test_title: PYST 24: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 13 Feb, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is '**in**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use with "reduction" is "**in**", which refers to a decrease within a category or measure.
 
• In the context of the sentence, "reduction in staff turnaround" implies a decrease in the rate at which staff are leaving or being replaced.
 
• "**In**" forms the correct collocation with "reduction" in formal English usage.
 
• Other options like "**at**", "**off**", and "**about**" do not fit grammatically or semantically in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Reducing the hours worked and optimising shift rostering could (1) **help __**alleviate stress, burnout and work family (2) __**conflict**__ for healthcare workers. All this is likely to improve staff retention. Any reduction (3) __**in**__ staff turnaround would save on direct costs associated (4) **________**hiring new staff. The cost to replace a highly specialised healthcare professional can reach up to 200% of their annual salary. Also, (5) **_________**shorter shifts may increase the uptake of shift times that are usually hard to fill. Measures like shorter shifts could also appeal to part time workers or those who have retired.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "At" is generally used for locations or points in time, not reductions.
 
• "Off" implies separation or detachment, which doesn't suit the meaning of decrease in staff turnover.
 
• "About" refers to topics or approximations and does not convey reduction accurately in this context.
